llm.summary: This Bilibili video helper is purpose-aligned, but its unsafe download command and unverified skill installation need review before use.

dimensions.detail: Downloading videos to the workspace is expected for this purpose, but the documented bash command interpolates dynamic path, filename, and URL values without robust quoting, URL validation, or an end-of-options marker.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill tells the agent to install doubao-video-analyze if missing, but does not specify a trusted source, publisher, pinned version, checksum, signature, or user approval step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation text starts with Bilibili-specific purpose but also says to invoke for video-content analysis requiring visual understanding, which could be interpreted broader than Bilibili-only use. The artifact also lacks strict validation for BV IDs or Bilibili hostnames before constructing commands.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact creates a workspace subdirectory and stores downloaded MP4 files there. It does not install services, hooks, memory rules, or other cross-session backdoors, but downloaded media persists until cleaned up.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently describes downloading a Bilibili video with yt-dlp and passing the local file to a video-analysis skill. The behavior fits the stated purpose, but it depends on user-provided video identifiers and URLs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a skill that downloads Bilibili videos into the workspace and may install another analysis skill. Before use, tighten the command handling: validate BV IDs and Bilibili HTTPS URLs, pass arguments without shell interpolation, add -- before the URL, and require explicit approval or a pinned trusted source for doubao-video-analyze.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Using yt-dlp is expected, but the exact shell command is under-scoped for hostile or malformed input because the URL is unquoted and the BV-derived filename is only double-quoted.
[T08] unexpected: A helper analysis skill may be purpose-aligned, but automatic installation by mutable name without provenance or pinning creates a supply-chain review concern.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The artifact is Bilibili-oriented, but the trigger language is broad enough to be invoked for generic video-analysis requests.
[SQP-3] expected: The artifact is written in Chinese, but it does not clearly force all user interaction into Chinese; this is a minor usability and scope note rather than a security concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Creating a local video directory and downloading an MP4 are expected for a video parser, but users should be aware it writes persistent media files and has no stated size limit or cleanup behavior.
